store.name: Palewick
store.tagline: Quiet things for the table, the bath and the shelf.
store.voice: Calm, plain and exact. Short sentences, concrete details (the clay, the weave, how long a candle burns), gentle humor at most. No hype, no exclamation marks, no 'curated' or 'elevated'. We describe how a thing is used and cared for, and let it be.
store.story: Palewick began in 2019 with one candle: undyed wax and a pale cotton wick, poured by Nora Wend in the old loading room of a paper mill in Ashby Falls, Vermont. Her friend Sam Avery, a former restaurant cook, wanted plates that looked right with any food, and found a family workshop in Portugal to throw them. The shop has grown slowly since, to about thirty things: stoneware, washed linen, glass, a few scents and small objects, each made by people we know and chosen to be used every day for years. The studio shop opens Thursday to Saturday; everything else ships from the room next door.

policies.refund:
If something isn't right, send it back within 30 days of delivery, unused and in its original packaging, and we will refund it in full to your original payment method.

Candles that have been burned, and soaps and bath soaks that have been opened, can't be returned, unless they arrived damaged.

If anything arrives broken or chipped, send us a photo at hello@palewick.example within 7 days and we will send a replacement or a refund straight away. You don't need to send the broken piece back.

To start a return, write to hello@palewick.example with your order number. Return shipping is $8, taken from your refund, or free if we made a mistake.
policies.shipping:
We ship to the United States and Canada. Orders leave our studio in Ashby Falls within two working days, packed in recycled paper with no plastic.

Standard shipping is $8 and free on orders over $100. Most US orders arrive in 3–6 working days and Canadian orders in 6–10. Canadian orders may be charged duties and taxes on delivery.

Subscriptions to beeswax tapers ship free.
policies.privacy:
We keep only what we need to send your order and answer your messages: your name, email, address and what you bought. Payments are handled by our payment provider; we never see or store your card number.

If you sign up for our letters, we use your email for them and nothing else; every letter has a link to unsubscribe. We never sell or share your information.

To see, correct or delete what we hold about you, write to hello@palewick.example.
policies.terms:
These terms apply when you buy from Palewick, 22 Mill Row, Ashby Falls, VT 05099.

Our stoneware and glass are made by hand, so sizes and glazes vary a little from piece to piece and from the photos. That is part of the work, not a fault.

Prices are in US dollars. We confirm every order by email, and the sale is complete when it ships. If a product turns out to be unavailable after you order, we refund it in full.

Subscriptions renew on their schedule until you skip or cancel them from your account, which you can do at any time before the next box ships.

Questions? Write to hello@palewick.example.

art_direction: Quiet, airy still-life and interior photography for a small shop of home goods. Ground: a pale fog-gray with a faint green cast, seamless and matte, the background of every product shot; rooms have pale gray-white limewashed walls, pale oak and pale stone surfaces. Light: soft, diffused northern daylight from one side, low contrast, gentle soft-edged shadows; never flash, harsh sun or orange golden-hour glow. Palette: fog gray, chalk white, pale sage, oat, soft slate and charcoal, raw linen and pale honey, with small touches of brushed brass; calm and desaturated. Composition: lots of negative space. Product shots show the object small to medium in the center of the frame, straight on or from a slight three-quarter angle, with at least a third of the frame empty around it. Scenes hold only a few objects: uncluttered, lived-in but tidy. Lens: a 50–85 mm look, true proportions, crisp texture of glaze, weave and wax, a fine natural grain. Real-photo style, minimal and calm. Avoid: any text, letters, numbers, logos, labels, stickers, tags, signage or watermarks (bottles, jars, boxes, books and soaps are completely blank); people and faces; clutter and piles of props; bright flowers; saturated or neon color; glossy plastic; a CGI look; heavy vignettes or dramatic shadows.

products.name: Fog Candle
products.description_html:
The candle we started with: undyed, poured by hand into a stoneware vessel you can keep long after. Each scent is quiet enough to fill a room without announcing itself.

Scents

  • Fig Leaf: green fig, cut stems, a little milk.
  • Cedar & Rain: wet stone, cedar, a cold window.
  • White Tea: pale tea, linen, a trace of pear.

Materials

Coconut and soy wax with an unbleached cotton wick, in a glazed stoneware vessel.

Care

Burn for two to three hours at a time and trim the wick to 1/4 in before you light it. Stop when 1/2 in of wax is left; wash the vessel with warm water and use it for pens or stems.

Dimensions

8 oz: 3.25 in across, 3.5 in tall, about 50 hours. 14 oz: 4 in across, 4 in tall, about 80 hours.

attributes.scent_notes: Fig Leaf, Cedar & Rain, White Tea
attributes.care: Trim the wick to 1/4 in; burn 2–3 hours at a time.

pages.title: About Palewick
pages.content_html:
Palewick began in 2019 with one candle: undyed wax, a pale cotton wick and a stoneware vessel you could keep afterwards. Nora poured the first batch in the old loading room of a paper mill on Mill Row, in Ashby Falls, Vermont. The name came from that wick.

Sam joined a year later. He had cooked in restaurants for a long time and wanted plates that looked right under any food, and that could go through a busy dishwasher every night for years. He found a family workshop in Portugal that throws stoneware the way he wanted it, iron-flecked with a soft satin glaze, and the table followed.

How we choose

We keep the shop small, about thirty things, and add slowly. Each piece has to be useful every day, made by people we know, and good enough to keep for a long time. If we wouldn't use it at home, we don't sell it.

Who makes it

Our stoneware comes from a third-generation pottery near Coimbra, our linen from a weaving mill in Lithuania, and our glass from a small glassworks that still blows every piece by mouth. Candles, sprays and soaps are made here in Ashby Falls, in small batches.

Visit

The studio shop at 22 Mill Row is open Thursday to Saturday, from 10 to 5. Orders are packed in the room next door.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content_html: We read every message and answer within one working day, usually sooner. For an order, please include its number; for a breakage, a photo helps us sort it out straight away.

pages.title: Shipping & returns
pages.content_html:
Shipping

We ship to the United States and Canada. Orders leave our studio within two working days, packed in recycled paper with no plastic.

  • Standard shipping is $8, and free on orders over $100.
  • Most US orders arrive in 3–6 working days; Canadian orders in 6–10.
  • Canadian orders may be charged duties and taxes on delivery.
  • Beeswax taper subscriptions always ship free.

Returns

Send anything back within 30 days of delivery, unused and in its packaging, for a full refund. Burned candles and opened soaps or bath soaks can't be returned.

To start a return, write to hello@palewick.example with your order number. Return shipping is $8, taken from your refund.

Breakages

If something arrives chipped or broken, send us a photo within 7 days. We'll send a replacement or a refund straight away, and you don't need to send the broken piece back.

pages.title: Questions
pages.content_html:
Is the stoneware dishwasher safe?

Yes. It is also safe in the oven up to 400°F. Avoid moving a hot plate straight into cold water.

Why does my plate look a little different from the photo?

Every piece is thrown and glazed by hand, so the flecks, the glaze and the size vary a little. No two are quite alike.

Do I need to iron the linen?

No. It is stone-washed to be soft and slightly creased. Shake it out after washing and dry it on the line or on low heat.

How do I get the most from a candle?

Burn it for two to three hours the first time, until the whole surface has melted, and trim the wick to 1/4 in before each lighting.

How does the taper subscription work?

A box of eight beeswax tapers arrives every two months for $27, shipped free. Skip a box or cancel any time from your account.

Do you wrap gifts?

Every order is wrapped in plain paper. Add a note at checkout and we'll write it by hand on a card.

posts.title: How to wash linen (and why we never iron it)
posts.content_html:
Linen has a reputation for being difficult. It isn't. It mostly wants to be left alone.

Washing

Wash it warm, not hot, with other linen or cotton of a similar color, and use a little less detergent than you think. Skip the fabric softener: it coats the fibers and makes them less absorbent.

Drying

Line drying is best, and the creases fall out as it hangs. If you use a dryer, keep it on low and take the linen out while it's still faintly damp. Fold it then, smoothing it with your hands.

Ironing

You can, while it's damp, on a hot setting. We don't. A slightly creased napkin looks like it belongs to someone, and a pressed one looks like it belongs to a hotel.

posts.title: A table for two on a Tuesday
posts.content_html:
We like a set table on an ordinary night. Not a dinner party, just the small difference between eating at a table and eating at a counter.

What it takes

  • Two low bowls: pasta, soup or a salad, all fit.
  • Two napkins, unironed.
  • Two glasses and a carafe of water, so nobody gets up.
  • One taper, lit before you sit down.

That's all. No runner, no centerpiece, no matching anything. Mix the glazes; they were made to go together.

Afterwards

Everything goes in the dishwasher except the carafe. The napkins go in with the towels on the weekend.

posts.title: Burning a candle well
posts.content_html:
A good candle can still burn badly. These three habits make it last longer and burn cleaner.

The first burn is the longest

Light it for two to three hours the first time, until the melted wax reaches the edge of the vessel. If you blow it out early, it will tunnel down the middle for the rest of its life.

Trim the wick

Before every lighting, trim the wick to about 1/4 in. A long wick smokes and flickers; a short one burns low and steady.

Know when to stop

When half an inch of wax is left, stop. Pour in hot water, let the wax float up and set, lift it out and wash the vessel. Ours make good homes for pens, brushes or a few stems.
